data.title: Missing consent "evidence" on contact form
data.body:
Currently, when an user submits a request through the Contact Form he/she's prompted to grant a consent to process the request thanks to the new plugin, so the user has to flag the checkbox to proceed. And that's ok, but site owner must be able to demonstrate that the user gave his/her consent to process the request/data. 

### Describe the solution you'd like
We could have two opportunities:

1. Add a copy of the consent statement in the email that is sent through the Contact Form.
2. Record the consent in the Consent view within Privacy Dashboard (index.php?option=com_privacy&view=consents)

data.body: Not really.  It would only be true if the plugin asking consent is enabled and all the pre-conditions involving that has been set.  Even then, that means hardcoding a plugin's configuration into a component, which is not proper system design (a component should not be aware of a specific plugin's presence at all).

data.title: Missing consent "evidence" on contact form
data.body:
I would see the situation in the following way: The spirit of GDPR is to make it obvious to the user what data a website collects about a person. In the case of a contact form, all data is provided by the user. So the consent of the user is given the moment that he typed it into the form. It is also not required that the user typed in real data. Long story short: For now I would say that the implicit consent was given when the contact form was filled out and the explicit consent was given when the checkbox was checked. That explicit consent is implicitly stored by the timestamp of the send mail.

So I would vote against coding anything into this and close this issue.

One thing that would also speak against storing this in Joomla would be, that sites without any interactive elements except for this contact form (like my own website for example) would then have to set up the whole privacy component. Right now a person could request all the data that I have about it and I would only have to go through the stuff on my local system. When you are storing this data in Joomla, you would have to provide that export, too.

So, nothing to do here, at least for now. We could revisit this issue when there are the first few decisions by courts.

data.title: Missing consent "evidence" on contact form
data.body:
Personally, i don't think we should store the consent in the Privacy dashboard.
Pursuant the Italian Law, before GDPR, there was a similar "consent" mechanism that each website should have implemented and generally it has been done through a checkbox at the end of the contact form (obviously people used third-party extensions to achieve this).
The checkbox was something similar to "I agree with the Privacy Policy of this website" and this sentence was copied also in the email sent to the administrator.
Something like this has been mandatory in Italy (at least) from several years. 
According to GDPR, consents must always be explicit, clear, with clear purpose and so on... so even if i agree with you that if i contact you, i'm implicitly consenting you to process the data i submit, it would be good, if we can add to the email the consent sentence.

data.title: Missing consent "evidence" on contact form
data.body:
> it would be good, if we can add to the email the consent sentence.

It would be nice.  Our system capabilities do not allow us to do so without hardcoding com_contact to be dependent on the single privacy consent plugin that we ship in core.  We do not have a hook to alter emails when they are being sent in core, and arbitrarily adding the string to the email would be factually incorrect if you do not have any form of consent in place when submitting it.

data.title: Missing consent "evidence" on contact form
data.body:
@jeckodevelopment
You can solve the problem by using the custom fields in this way ...

1 - Create a new group of "mail" type fields and name it "Privacy policy".

2 - Create a new additional field of type "mail" as follows:

Title > I declare that I have read and accepted the following Privacy policy

Type > Checkboxes

Required > Yes

Text > By sending us a message through this form, or by directly using the e-mail address indicated here, the processing of your personal data will be carried out in compliance with the EU Regulation 2016/679. The personal data you have provided may be processed in compliance with the aforementioned legislation. The Data Controller, in compliance with the Regulations, will take care of archiving for purposes consistent with the interactions shown by the Visitor and only for the time strictly necessary for the verification and evaluation of the information provided, for the purpose of exchanging information or contacts. To find out more about our privacy policies, please see the extended information at https://www.XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX/privacy. To request information, changes, or to oppose the treatment and request the cancellation of your data, present in our archives, you can write to us via the address XXXXXXXXXX@XXXXXXX.XX.

Value > The same policy entered in Text

Field Group > Assign the previously created group "Privacy policy".

Go to the Permissions tab and set this...
Edit Custom Field Value > Allowed

In this way, the privacy policy will be visible on the contact page, but will also be contained in the email.
